title: Introduce operator-bound KMS proofs, audit-entropy throttle, and RBACv2 soft-guard
author: Anjali Rao
release_notes: Adds operator-scoped KMS attestation, RBACv2 soft-guard (shadow enforcement), and an audit-entropy throttle. Opt-in via config; no default behavior changes.
body:
Motivation: Customers operating in regulated environments require non-repudiable proof that human/operator-driven actions (deploys, secret grants, manual key rotations) were authorized and executed by specific operator principals and that audit exports do not leak high-entropy payloads at scale. This PR introduces a tied set of changes: (1) operator-bound KMS proofs — ephemeral KMS-wrapped attestations that prove an operator performed an action; (2) an audit-entropy throttle — a configurable sampler/transform that reduces frequency of full payload audit exports while preserving cryptographic anchors; and (3) RBACv2 soft-guard — a shadow-deny mode that enforces rules in detection-only mode with throttling and operator proof gating.

What this delivers: single-digit surface changes that compose into an end-to-end compliance capability: - OperatorActions API header (X-Operator-Proof) populated by the operator client when performing elevated operations; servers verify KMS-wrapped proofs and log verification results to audit. - New KMS attestor component that generates short-lived attestations tied to operator identity and the service action hash; designed to work with multiple KMS backends via existing KMS abstraction. - Audit service: entropy_throttle module that inspects event types and payload entropy markers, applies configurable sampling rates per tenant/route, attaches a compact cryptographic anchor (SHA256 sig) and optionally stores full payloads in a tenant-scoped cold bucket if requested. - RBACv2 soft-guard hook added to policy decision point (PDP) to emit shadow-deny metrics, rate-limit denials per operator, and optionally require operator-proof verification for deny-elevating operations.

Design notes: - Proof format: {version:1, op_hash, operator_id, ts, kms_sig} wrapped in the existing KMS envelope; verification is a fast path that uses KMS public keys cached with TTL. Proofs expire after 5 minutes; replay protection uses op_hash which includes request nonce + body hash. - Entropy throttle: tenants can configure per-route thresholds (default: full capture for admin routes, 0.1% capture for high-volume webhook routes). Throttled events still include an audit anchor and proof-of-injection metadata for future retrieval. - Soft-guard: default off; when enabled it does not block requests but writes a denial_event to audit with severity and increments the enforcement scoreboard. This lets SRE/security tune rules without user impact.

Implementation summary (single continuous string describing files below): key changes across services: KMS adapter additions, authz PDP extension, audit service module, API surface for operator clients, unit and integration tests, docs and rollout script.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for KMS attestor and proof verification added (coverage ~92% for new modules). - Integration test scenario: simulated operator performing a key-rotate; server verifies proof, audit records full payload (since admin route), and soft-guard produced no deny by default. - Load test: entropy throttle sampled at 0.5% under synthetic webhook traffic (100k/s) and reduced audit storage by ~220x while anchors were preserved. - CI: local lint/build/test passed; two flaky acceptance tests required one rerun in CI.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy KMS attestor with feature flag disabled; 2) Enable proof verification in audit pipeline as observability-only (no blocking); 3) Invite a pilot tenant to opt-in for full operator-proof capturing; 4) Gradual ramp for entropy throttle defaults on high-volume routes; 5) Enable soft-guard for selected policy sets, monitor scoreboard and error budgets for two weeks, then consider hard enforcement.

Checklist: - [x] KMS attestor implementation and abstraction - [x] Proof verification middleware - [x] Audit entropy_throttle + anchors - [x] PDP soft-guard hook + metrics - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs: operator guide and compliance notes - [x] Rollout script and feature-flag gating

Risk & mitigations: - Risk: misconfigured throttle could drop too many events. Mitigation: default conservative sampling, dashboard shows per-route capture rates and raw retrieval interface. - Risk: performance regression on authz path. Mitigation: proof verification uses cached KMS pubkeys and a fast verify path; added benchmark shows <0.6ms median overhead.

Related work: builds on ENG-4123 (KMS adapter migration) and SEC-61 (RBACv2 telemetry).

review_comments: Marcus Liu (reviewer): Can the attestor support multiple KMS backends per-tenant (yes/no)? - Comment: we should document the failure mode when primary KMS is unavailable.
Anjali Rao (author): Reply: yes — adapter already supports multiple providers; added fallback logic and test. Failure modes documented in docs/compliance/operator-proofs.md.
Priya Patel (reviewer): Request change: throttle config shape is complex, please add a simple default schema and a CLI helper to validate tenant config.
Anjali Rao (author): Done — added validation helper and a short 'howto' in deploy/featureflags/operator_proof.yaml.
Diego Moreno (reviewer): Minor: add metric for proof verification latency and a histogram bucket to monitoring dashboard.
Anjali Rao (author): Added metric pkg/metrics/softguard_scoreboard.go and exported histogram; updated dashboards PR reference in release notes.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: features are behind feature flags and opt-in per-tenant. Security team performed an architecture review (SEC-88) prior to merge.
